messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO burn detected for service=redwood-serving, metric=serving.latency.p95, windows=[5m:170%, 1h:55%], severity=critical, region=us-west-2. Paging criteria matched. Pager: @oncall. Link: https://pager.example/INC-1472
Alex P: I'm on it. seeing elevated p95 on the canary and prod pools. Not seeing obvious spike in qps.
Nina R: heads-up — customers on dedicated instances reporting slow responses via support channel.
Jamal: attaching a quick query I ran: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,job))
```
Jamal: 5m window shows several nodes at 700-900ms p95, baseline is ~120ms.
Megan L: any recent deploys? I don't see deploy bot triggers in the last 30m.
Alex P: no deploys. I SSH'd into one of the affected hosts — CGO logs show repeated GC stalls and sporadic high CPU in the inference runtime.
OpsRunbookBot: runbook reference: /runbooks/serving/latency-p95. Steps: check backlog, restart worker, check kernel/memory.
Nina R: quick mitigation: let's scale up inference pool in us-west-2 by +2 pods (temporary) and disable batching window on canary to cut latency. Who can execute?
Alex P: I can scale now. bumping target replicas and forcing immediate scaling.
Alex P: scaled +2, disabling batching on canary (config id: canary-batch-2026).
Jamal: after scale: p95 dropped to ~250ms in 10m. good sign. 1h burn still elevated though.
Megan L: recommended next: create a short-term alert suppression for noisy tokenization errors while we stabilize, but keep paging on for sustained burn-rate (1h).
Nina R: Agreed. We need to avoid reflexive paging on transient 5m spikes. Proposal: change paging rule to require both: (5m burn >= 150% AND 1h burn >= 40%) OR (5m burn >= 1000% for immediate pager). Thoughts?
Alex P: +1 on multi-window combined gating. Less noise, still catches real incidents. Let's also add a 10m window for intermediate detection.
Jamal: suggestion: use a simple boolean expression in our alert rule: ```yaml
expr: (burn_rate_5m >= 1.5 and burn_rate_1h >= 0.4) or (burn_rate_5m >= 10)
for: 2m
labels:
  pager: "true"
```
Megan L: I want to avoid dropping visibility — create a non-paging alert channel for 5m-only spikes so product/eng can see but not be paged. Use #eng-notifications for those.
Nina R: action items: 1) Adjust paging rule as Jamal suggested. 2) Add 5m non-pager alert to #eng-notifications. 3) Build a dashboard panel that shows multi-window burn comparison (5m / 10m / 1h). 4) Update runbook to call out scaling vs restart thresholds. Who picks these up?
Alex P: I'll open INC-1472 and attach the metric snapshots and mitigation steps.
Jamal: I'll put together the alert PR for prometheus-alerts repo with the YAML change. Assign to @Megan for review.
Megan L: I'll review and also create the dashboard in Grafana. I'll add panel queries and a quick note on when to scale vs restart.
OpsRunbookBot: note: recommended paging budget policy: allow one 5m pager in a 6h window before requiring human confirmation for automatic paging.
Nina R: let's not be too strict there — some customer-impacting bursts should still page. propose: automatic paging max 2 per 6h, then require manual confirm for further pages for same SLO.
Alex P: fine with that. update runbook to show '2 automatic pages per 6h' and 'after 2, escalate to oncall lead for judgement'.
Jamal: logging follow-up: add a sampling trace for GC logs to correlate with p95 spikes. I'll open a separate ticket.
Megan L: Customer comms: support flagged 4 customers affected; we should prepare a short status note once we stabilize. I'll draft.
Alex P: thanks everyone. current status: mitigated (scaled + batching change), monitoring. I'll keep a watch for 2h.
Nina R: postmortem checklist: metric timeline, dashboard link, alert PR link, runbook edit, root cause hypothesis (GC backpressure + batching interaction).
Megan L: I'll post the draft status and link to the incident thread in #customer-success.
Jamal: PR for alert rule at https://git.example/alerts/merge/987 — please review.
Alex P: closing pager for now; marking incident as "stabilized". Please still comment on the ticket if you see regression. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-1472 status updated -> stabilized by Alex P. Duration: 52m.
Megan L: post-incident tasks assigned: Alex (monitor), Jamal (alerts PR), Megan (dash & comms), Nina (runbook update). I'll create a follow-up in the SRE board for tuning review next week.
Nina R: one more note — recommend adding an alert annotation with 'suggested actions' so responders see the gating logic and quick runbook links in the alert. small UX win.
Alex P: agreed. I'll add that to the PR.
Megan L: thanks team. good job reacting quickly.
